title: A Bell in the Snow

plate.narration: A little snowhorn goat bleats across the meltwater. Its herd answers from a snowy ledge, bells clinking. Between them, the water runs cold and quick. Those small hooves need a way home.

goal.text: Get the little goat home safe and find somewhere warm.

steps.label: Get the goat back to its herd
Get everyone in from the cold

arrival.narration: The bell rings again. The kid answers with an enormous bleat for such a small goat. You brush snow from its knees, scraped in the scramble on the quay. Across the slope, a herd of snowhorn goats waits on a ledge. A bell hangs from one goat's collar. Between you and the herd, a melt channel cuts through the snow. Your job is plain: get the little goat home to its herd, then find somewhere warm for everyone.

choices.label: Look for a safe way to the herd

shelter.narration: Wind presses your wet clothes against your knees. The kid is shivering. A bank of packed snow would block the wind; a row of dark rocks would lead you nearer the bell. What do you do first?

choices.label: Make a windbreak in the snow
Follow the dark rocks
Use Mend to warm the kid's scraped knees

windbreak.narration: You scrape a hollow behind the bank and huddle shoulder to shoulder. The kid noses under the warmest arm. From here you can see footprints between the dark rocks, each wider than your head.

choices.label: Stamp and wring until the shivers stop

rocks.narration: The rocks give your feet something firm to find under the snow. Beside them are deep footprints. A broad wooden sledge has scraped a second track toward the bell.

choices.label: Warm up behind the rocks

mend.narration: Gentle light settles over the kid's scraped knees. It stops shaking long enough to chew the end of your sleeve. You tuck it back into your coat and find broad footprints between the rocks.

choices.label: Warm up before you move on

wind_warm.prompt: Everyone wring out your wet things and flap them until the ice flakes off.
wind_warm.narration: The wind finds every wet seam in your clothes. Your sleeves have started to crackle. The kid sneezes a tiny cloud. Nobody climbs a glacier with stiff fingers.

onSuccess.narration: The ice cracks off in crumbs. You are damp, not frozen, and the kid sneezes in triumph. The wind has less to bite now.

onFailure.narration: One sleeve freezes into a stiff tube, and it takes three tries to bend it. You get going, but your fingers ache.

kid_burrow.narration: The kid wriggles out of your coat, warm enough now to be cheeky. It dives under a snow mound and vanishes. Three mounds sit in a row, all exactly the same shape. Then the snow starts to move.

interaction.cue: Watch the mound the kid hides under, then pick where it is.

onSuccess.narration: There it is! The kid pops up wearing a snow hat and lets out an enormous bleat. You tuck it back into your coat.

onFailure.narration: You lift an empty mound. A snowy nose pokes out of another one and sneezes. You scoop the kid back into your coat.

onAssisted.narration: You line up the mounds and listen. A tiny bleat gives it away, and the kid goes back in your coat.

prints.narration: Past the rocks, the snow is stamped with big footprints, each one wide as a dinner plate. The wind is filling them in as fast as it can. Some lead toward the bell. Some wander off as if the walker forgot where they were going. Which line do you trust?

choices.label: Look for the freshest prints
Follow the line at a quick march
Use skyward or glide to look down at the whole trail

prints_read.prompt: Whoever has the sharpest eyes finds the freshest line of prints.
prints_read.narration: Fresh prints have sharp edges. Old ones are soft as pillows. You crouch and squint, and squinting helps a little.

onSuccess.narration: Sharp edges, fresh snow. The line bends toward the bell, and you follow it.

onFailure.narration: You follow a line that ends at a bare patch where the walker clearly sat down to think. You backtrack, grumbling, and find the right line.

prints_march.prompt: Everyone march along the prints before the wind fills them in.
prints_march.narration: Left foot in the first print, right foot in the next. The prints are far apart, so it is like hopping across a giant's stepping stones.

onSuccess.narration: Print by print you hop along, and the line leads toward the bell.

onFailure.narration: A foot misses a print and sinks to the knee. Everyone stops to dig that boot out, and the line almost vanishes. You catch it just in time.

prints_air.prompt: Use skyward or glide to look down at the whole trail. The hero with wings helps; choose who leads.
prints_air.narration: A griffin can rise above the wind and see a whole trail at once. A dragonling can glide a little way up and look. From above, the prints draw a line toward the bell.

onSuccess.narration: From up high the line is plain, and you point everyone along it.

onFailure.narration: The wind tosses the view into a swirl. You come down and follow your nose instead, and it mostly works.

tracks.narration: A yeti herder comes around the ridge pulling an empty sledge. She stops at the sight of the kid. "There you are." Then she notices the rest of you. "There you all are. Did you come with the weather?"

choices.label: Tell her about the fold on the quay
Ask for help getting the kid home

variants.text: She looks back at your line of stones. "You marked the hollow. That will help the next person through."
She checks the kid with one broad hand. "Still warm. That long way round was well chosen."
You point out the hollow behind you. She nods. "And you found your own way out. Keep that rope."

tell_rift.narration: The yeti looks at your wet boots, then at the harbor rope. "The Exchange," she says. "That is a long way to arrive without a hat." She lays a folded blanket on the sledge. "Stand on the dark ice when I say. Walk around the white patches."

choices.label: Walk with her to the channel

ask_help.narration: "First we get you warm enough to help," says the yeti. She takes a folded blanket from the sledge and wraps it around the kid and your arms together. "I keep this herd. The glacier keeps surprising me." She turns the sledge toward the melt channel.

choices.label: Walk with her to the channel

herder_gift.narration: At the channel's edge the herder stops and looks you over. "I saw you leave my tin tidy," she says. "Keep the coins. I leave them for whoever needs them, and today that was you." She digs in the sledge and hands over a bundle wrapped in a cloth. "Bread, cheese, and a sausage that has not made up its mind. You are thin as icicles." She points across the water. "The herd is over there, and the snow bridge looks tired. First we read the ice. Then we cross."

choices.label: Read the ice with her

read_water.prompt: Whoever reads ice best picks out the edges that will hold.
read_water.narration: Along the channel the ice comes in two kinds. One looks dark and wet and holds a boot. The other looks like sugar and holds nothing at all. The herder waits to see what you see.

onSuccess.narration: You trace a line of dark ice along the bank, and the herder nods at every patch you pick.

onFailure.narration: You point at a sugar patch. The herder's boot goes through it with a crunch, and she hops out with one very cold foot. "That one taught us both," she says. You look again and find the dark line.

channel.narration: Meltwater gurgles through a narrow gap. The nearest snow bridge sags when the yeti tests it. A flat stone projects farther upstream. The herder points out dark patches of ice that will hold a careful foot. The herd waits on the other side, bells clinking.

choices.label: Use the stepping stone
Make a bridge with the sledge
Carry a rope across on wings
Keep everyone in step with a steady song

step.prompt: Step across the stone without slipping into the meltwater.

onSuccess.narration: You land on the far bank and pass the kid across.

onFailure.narration: Your foot slips into icy water. The herder catches your wrist and lifts you onto the bank.

sledge.prompt: Hold the sledge steady while everyone crosses.

onSuccess.narration: You brace the runners against the stone. The party crawls over one at a time.

onFailure.narration: A runner slips. The herder grabs the sledge and you scramble across, soaked to the elbows.

wing_line.prompt: Wings carry the rope to the far bank. Can you guide the loose line around the sharp ice?

onSuccess.narration: You guide the line clear of sharp ice. Secured around a rock on the far bank, it steadies everyone crossing.

onFailure.narration: The line snags on sharp ice. You free it, splashing one foot into the channel.

song_step.prompt: A Songkeeper sets a steady pace. Can you lead the party along the dark patches in time with the song?

onSuccess.narration: You call the steps in time with the song. Each friend follows the herder's safe footholds.

onFailure.narration: Your foot slips between two beats. The herder pulls you clear and leads the last steps herself.

dry_bank.narration: The kid sees the herd and wriggles free. A shaggy goat sniffs it from nose to tail, then nudges it firmly between her front legs. The herder checks every one of you before she smiles. "All back. Good."

choices.label: Help settle the herd

wet_bank.narration: The herder wrings the edge of your sleeve out over the channel. "We will dry that indoors." The kid has already run to a shaggy goat, who sniffs it all over and refuses to let it move.

choices.label: Help the herd settle

settle.narration: The herd crowds around the kid, bells clanking like a kitchen drawer. A shaggy lead goat with one chipped horn sniffs each of you in turn. Behind her the others jostle, wet and cross. "They will not go indoors while they are upset," says the herder. "Settle them, and they will walk in by themselves."

choices.label: Count the goats by their bells
Brush the ice from their wool
Give the lead goat your supper
Use a lullaby to calm the herd

settle_count.prompt: Whoever counts best names every goat by its bell.
settle_count.narration: Every goat has a different bell: a clank, a tink, a cowbell, a spoon on a pot. The herd keeps moving, and counting moving goats is like counting raindrops.

onSuccess.narration: Every bell is here, even the spoon one. The herder checks your count against hers and smiles. The goats calm down, because someone finally knows who they are.

onFailure.narration: You count one goat twice and one goat not at all, and the herder has to start over. The goats grumble, but the count comes out right in the end.

settle_brush.prompt: Everyone pick a goat and brush the ice from its wool.
settle_brush.narration: Goat wool freezes into little ice beads that rattle when the goats walk. Each bead is cold on the goat and colder on you. The goats hold still for brushing, as long as you find the itchy spot.

onSuccess.narration: The beads come off in handfuls, and the goats lean into your hands. Soon the herd sounds like a rattle full of calm.

onFailure.narration: Some goats like the brush and some goats bite the brush. A mouthful of mitten later, everyone is mostly brushed.

settle_feed.narration: You unwrap the supper. The lead goat sniffs the cheese, sniffs the bread, and sneezes. Then she eats the crust and gives you a long, forgiving look. She turns around, and the whole herd follows her, bell by bell, to where the herder is waiting. Your pockets are lighter. The goats are not upset anymore.

choices.label: Go with the herd

settle_lull.prompt: Use a lullaby to calm the herd. The songkeeper helps; choose who leads.
settle_lull.narration: A songkeeper hums a slow tune that sounds like a blanket. The lead goat's ears droop. The spoon bell goes quiet.

onSuccess.narration: The song rolls over the herd. One by one the goats stop stamping and follow the tune toward the herder.

onFailure.narration: The song is lovely, but the wind is loud. The goats settle anyway, slowly, with their eyes shut.

herd_play.narration: The goats are calmer, and the herder is counting hay. The kid stands in the middle of the herd with its ears up, and every goat wants a turn at fussing over it. The lead goat sniffs the air. She is waiting to see what you will do.

options.label: Brush a goat's wool
options.reaction: A goat leans into the brush until it nearly tips over.

options.label: Scratch the kid behind the ears
options.reaction: The kid shuts its eyes and makes a happy, wobbly bleat.

options.label: Offer a handful of hay
options.reaction: The lead goat takes the hay politely and chews with great dignity.

onSuccess.narration: The whole herd settles around you with a clank of bells. The lead goat gives you one slow, approving blink.

onFailure.narration: The goats settle a little at a time, and the herder waits patiently for the last stragglers.

onAssisted.narration: The herder shows you a good scratching spot, and the herd settles around it.

herd.narration: The herder calls the goats toward a low opening in the ice. The kid plants its feet at the entrance. From inside comes a deep note that trembles through your boots. How do you coax it in?

choices.label: Sit beside it and wait
Let it follow a friend's sleeve
Hum back to the low note

patient.narration: You sit in the snow beside the kid. The herd keeps walking. At last it butts your elbow, gets up, and trots after them. The herder waits for you too.

choices.label: Go inside together

sleeve.narration: You offer a loose cuff. The kid gives it an interested nibble. The kid takes the end in its mouth and follows you through the doorway. "That coat has earned its keep," says the herder.

choices.label: Follow the sound

hum.narration: You hum the low note. The kid tilts its head. From inside the ice, another voice hums back. The kid follows the sound, and you follow the kid.

choices.label: Meet whoever answered

hall.narration: The doorway opens into a singing hall carved from ice. Yetis sit on benches around warm cups, holding one low note together. The herder drapes your wet things near a row of warm stones and pours tea. Damp blankets hang over a rail. "Glacier of Origins," she says. "You may stop arriving now." At the back of the hall, warm air drifts out of a glass door, and someone inside is singing scales.

choices.label: Sit at the long table by the warm stones
Follow the warm air to the glass door

hall_table.narration: The herder points you to a long table beside the warm stones. At the end of it, a round yeti knitter is making a scarf so long it runs under the bench and out the other side. She holds up a hank of boot laces woven from goat wool. "Three coins a pair. Quickest laces on the glacier," she says. "Or sit and be warm for free. I do not charge for sitting." Your boots are still soggy.

choices.label: Dry your boots on the warm stones
Buy a pair of woven laces for 3 coins
Share your supper with the knitter

hall_dry.narration: You line your boots up on the warm stones and wiggle your toes. Steam rises from the leather, and a small pond runs out of each toe. The knitter hangs your socks on her scarf, which is what the scarf is for. The herder pours another cup.

choices.label: Warm up and listen to the hall

variants.text: You line your boots up on the warm stones and wiggle your toes. The dry crossing paid off, because they are only damp, and the steam is gone in a minute. The knitter hangs your socks on her scarf, which is what the scarf is for. The herder pours another cup.

hall_buy.narration: You count three coins into the knitter's mitten. She ties the laces into your boots with a speedy bow, and the knots feel snug and springy. "Go on, run," she says. "Do not trip. They are fast laces."

choices.label: Warm up and listen to the hall

hall_share.narration: You break the supper in two and hand the knitter the bigger half. She eats the sausage first, politely. Then she hands over a small whistle carved from a goat horn. "For calling a herd off thin snow," she says. "One loud note. Do not blow it indoors."

choices.label: Warm up and listen to the hall

conservatory.narration: Behind the glass door is a greenhouse, warm and damp and full of song. This school is called the Conservatory. Here students learn to be a Songkeeper, a hero who heals with songs. A yeti named Aunt Bellow conducts with a carrot. Her students sing in a row, and every plant in the room leans toward whoever is singing best. Right now the ferns lean toward a very small frogfolk at the end. Above the door hangs a song bell on a cord. A Songkeeper's songs live in that bell, and it will not ring near a thorn bracer. "Anyone who wants the bell," says Aunt Bellow, "may try it on."

variants.text: Aunt Bellow waves her carrot. "Back to the Conservatory? Good." Every plant turns, slowly, to see who has come in. The song bell waits above the door for anyone who wants to try it on.

choices.label: Sing for the plants
Back to the singing hall

conservatory_sing.narration: Aunt Bellow points her carrot at you. You sing. A sunflower turns its whole head to look. Then a fern. Then, very slowly, a shy little cactus. Aunt Bellow writes something on a leaf. "The cactus never turns," she whispers. "Keep singing."

choices.label: Back to the singing hall

listen.narration: A young yeti stops singing to turn a page in an open songbook. The note thins. Another singer joins, and it fills the hall again. The herder taps the bench beside her. "Low and steady. Try it. Nobody here learned by already knowing."

choices.label: Learn the note with the yetis
Ask what the song is for

song_answer.narration: "For listening," says the herder. She puts a hand against the wall. "A crack makes one sound. Running water makes another. The song helps us hear the difference." She hums the note once and waits for you to answer.

choices.label: Hum the note back

note_try.narration: The low note is lower than your voice wants to go. The young yeti singer taps a spot on the floor. "Stand here. Hum from your boots."

interaction.cue: Listen to the young singer, then hum the pattern back.

onSuccess.narration: Your voices lock together like the teeth of a comb. The whole bench rumbles, and the young singer grins.

onFailure.narration: Your note slides up and down like a goat on ice. The young singer shows you where to put your tongue, and the second try wobbles into place.

onAssisted.narration: The young singer hums it slowly beside you, one step at a time, until your voices settle.

learn_note.narration: You find the note together. At first it shakes; then your voices settle. Across the hall, frost trembles off a sealed seam in the wall. The herder lays a palm on it, listening. "That seam was quiet yesterday."

choices.label: Listen to the seam

changing.narration: "The melt is early," the herder says. "A path we used last week is water now. It led to the herd's sheltered grazing ledge. We are using stored hay while we find another way, and the pile gets smaller every day." She looks at the sealed seam. "Perhaps listening will tell us where it is safe to look." Outside, a bell rings twice. Three travelers in dark cloaks are packing their camp beside the hall.

choices.label: Help the herder dry the last blankets
Walk out toward the travelers' camp

variants.text: "Your windbreak is useful too," she adds. "I can tell the next travelers where to stop if the weather turns."
"And thank you for keeping everyone steady at the channel. I cannot watch every crossing now."

blankets.narration: You spread the last blanket over a rail. The herder packs a dry corner around your rope. "Bring it back if you pass this way. Bring yourselves back too." The kid bumps your knee before returning to the herd.

choices.label: Walk out toward the travelers' camp

ledge_look.narration: The herder leads you past the end of the hall, where the ground drops to a stream. A path ran here last week. Now meltwater nibbles the snow shelf along its bank, and the shelf looks like it is deciding whether to fall in. "The herd will not walk where it cannot see poles," she says. "And the hay must go down to the lower pen before dark. I have two jobs and one sledge."

choices.label: Push poles into the snow to mark the safe line
Haul the hay sledge down to the lower pen
Use brace to hold the snow shelf steady
Blow the goat-horn whistle to clear the thin snow

ledge_poles.prompt: Everyone grab a pole and plant a line along the safe edge.
ledge_poles.narration: The poles are long and the wind is nosy. Each one has to go in straight, or the goats will follow it straight into the stream.

onSuccess.narration: A row of poles marches down the bank, crooked as skinny dancers. The herd can see where to walk.

onFailure.narration: One pole goes in soft and leans like a tired flag. Your fingers freeze, but you straighten it, and then you straighten all the others too.

ledge_hay.prompt: The strongest of you takes the front of the sledge while the others push.
ledge_hay.narration: The hay sledge is heavy as a sleeping bear and slides like a happy one.

onSuccess.narration: The sledge glides down the slope with a hiss. The pile at the lower pen grows by a whole sledge's worth.

onFailure.narration: The sledge gets away from you and slides to the bottom on its own, scattering hay. You collect most of it. The goats help, which means they eat some.

ledge_brace.prompt: Use brace to hold the snow shelf steady while the poles go in. The hero with brace helps; choose who leads.
ledge_brace.narration: A thornguard can plant both feet and hold. The snow shelf creaks, and the thornguard does not.

onSuccess.narration: The shelf stops creaking, and the poles go in, one by one, in a straight row.

onFailure.narration: The shelf shifts under the brace, but the poles still go in. Everyone works fast and nobody breathes.

ledge_whistle.narration: You blow one loud note. Every goat in the herd lifts its head. They turn and walk off the thin snow in a line, bells clanking, and the herder does not have to say a word. "Well," she says. "That is a better whistle than mine." She plants the poles herself while the goats watch.

choices.label: See what is left to do

shelf_cross.narration: One last pole waits on the far side of the snow shelf, where the stream keeps nibbling. The herder points at the water. "It pauses between gulps. Step across when it goes quiet." The stream gulps. The stream goes quiet.

interaction.cue: Step across when the water goes quiet.

onSuccess.narration: You step across in the quiet, plant the pole, and hop back before the next gulp. The herd watches without a single bell.

onFailure.narration: The stream gulps early and takes a bite out of the snow shelf, but you skip aside. The herder plants the pole herself.

onAssisted.narration: The herder counts the gulps aloud, and you cross on the count. The pole goes in.

ledge_done.narration: The herder looks over the stream, the herd, the hay and the line of safe ground. The shelf still groans, but no goat is on it. "The glacier is changing," she says. "But it will not catch us today." Past the hall, the travelers wave from their camp. "Go on. And thank you."

choices.label: Go and meet the travelers

departure.narration: Warm and dry, you step out beside the singing hall. The kid stays with its herd. A griffin in a travel cloak is trying to fold a map while a unicorn stands on one corner. Neither has noticed that the corner is under her hoof.

variants.text: The herder lifts a hand from the newly cleared blanket rail. "Dry blankets for the next arrivals. That matters."

drift.narration: A gust wipes the footprints smooth. Ahead, a white drift fills the gap between two ridges of dark rock. The bell sounds from beyond it, but you cannot see how deep the snow is. The kid shivers against your chest. How will you get everyone through?

choices.label: Use the rope to test the drift and mark firm ground
Keep the kid tucked in and go around the rocks
Try the last place you saw the footprints

drift_probe.narration: You knot the rope around a rock and move a few steps at a time. Beneath a thin crust, the drift is hollow. You back out, find firm ground along its edge, and leave small stones marking the safe way. Beyond the ridge, the bell rings louder.

choices.label: Go on

drift_detour.narration: You take turns sheltering the kid inside your coats while you follow the rocks around the drift. The walk is longer, but nobody has to test the hidden hollow. At the far ridge the kid stops shaking and pokes its nose out toward the bell.

choices.label: Go on

drift_slip.narration: The crust gives under your first step. You sink to your knees, still holding the kid above the snow. Your party lays the rope across firm rock, and you pull yourself back along it. Now you can see the hollow. You skirt its edge and reach the next ridge together.

choices.label: Go on

crust_hold.narration: At the foot of the next ridge, the path squeezes under a lip of snow that sags over the stones like a heavy white eyebrow. The kid is small enough to pass. The rest of you are not, unless somebody holds the snow up.

interaction.cue: Hold the snow up while your friend carries the kid under.

onSuccess.narration: The snow lip stays up, and the kid trots under it. Then it trots back under it, just to check.

onFailure.narration: The lip sags and sheds a heap of snow. You dig a gap with your hands, and the kid squeezes through with a snort.

onAssisted.narration: You wedge your rope and some stones under the lip. It holds, and everyone gets through.

cairn.narration: Past the drift, a tall pile of stones stands at the foot of the ridge, taller than the kid and much neater. A flat tin lid peeks out of the snow beneath it, stamped with a little bell. Somebody left it here on purpose, and the wind has been trying to bury it.

choices.label: Dig the tin out together
Pry the lid loose with a stick and your rope
Use smash to crack the ice off the lid

cairn_dig.prompt: Everyone dig at the tin with both hands and heave.
cairn_dig.narration: The snow is packed hard, and the tin is frozen to the ground. The kid helps by digging, badly.

onSuccess.narration: The tin pops out like a cork. Nobody falls over, which is lucky for the kid.

onFailure.narration: The tin comes loose all at once and everyone sits down in the snow. Your hands sting, but the lid is free.

cairn_pry.prompt: Whoever is cleverest works out where the stick and the rope should go.
cairn_pry.narration: You slide the stick under one edge of the lid and loop the rope around it. Pulling is the easy part. Knowing where is the hard part.

onSuccess.narration: You hook the rope under the lid and lean. It pops with a crack.

onFailure.narration: The stick snaps. You use your fingernails instead, and the lid gives up in the end.

cairn_smash.prompt: Use smash to crack the ice off the lid. The hero with smash helps; choose who leads.
cairn_smash.narration: A bigfoot can break a barrier with one good whack. The ice around the lid is thick, and the whack is thicker.

onSuccess.narration: One thump and the ice falls off in plates. The lid rattles loose.

onFailure.narration: The first thump bounces off. The second makes the whole pile wobble, and you catch it just in time.

cairn_open.narration: Inside the tin are four coins, a stub of candle, and a note with a drawing of a bell. The note says, "For whoever is lost when the weather turns. Buy something warm. Leave the tin." You take the coins and tuck the tin back under the stones. The kid tries to eat the candle. Beyond the ridge, something creaks.

choices.label: Go see what is creaking

seam_response.narration: The note fades. So does the trembling under the herder's palm. A narrow line of frost has fallen to the floor beneath the sealed seam. You still remember the note. What do you try?

choices.label: Hum the note again
Rest a hand on the ice while the others hum
Ask the herder to listen with you

seam_hum.narration: You hum. Frost ticks down the seam in time with the note. You stop; the ticking stops. When you begin again, it answers again. The ice stays shut. The herder brings her cup over and sits beside you. "Well. That was not an accident."

choices.label: Go on

seam_touch.narration: You rest your hand flat on the ice. As the others hum, a faint tremble reaches your palm. It fades when they stop. You try twice more and get the same answer. The seam stays shut. "Something we can test," says the herder.

choices.label: Go on

seam_listen.narration: The herder kneels beside you. You take turns humming and listening. Each time the note sounds, a low ticking answers from the seam. "We can hear that much," she says. "What lies beyond it, I do not know." The ice stays shut.

choices.label: Go on

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny, curious, with real consequences. Describe actions and sensory details directly. Short dialogue. Never use "the kind of thing that", "the sort of thing that", or "it was X, the type of thing that makes you Y" comparisons. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.

npcVoices.Yeti herder: Chapter-scoped female yeti herder and singer. Patient, dry humor, practical cold-weather care. Gives no complete history, prison hints, or explanation of the rifts.
npcVoices.Young yeti singer: Learns and listens; no lore lecture.
